title: Hillcrest Dairies program on WWL staff orchestra
summary: Netto describes the cellist, playing tuba in the photo, and the Sunday half-hour Hillcrest Dairies program on WWL that paid about $6, dating it to before 1934 and the 1932 bank closings.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It was Marcel Dorman, one of the finest in the country. He had that reputation. But he's known to Yo-Yo Ma, I don't think. And that's Al Fisher Hill. On bass. Yeah, on the bass. In other words, I took the tuba and took the picture with the tuba, so make room here. But that was a combination. This was the Hillcrest office. We used to play a program for them every Sunday. On WWL. On WWL, yeah. The staff orchestra.
Yeah, they used to be the Hillcrest Farms and the Hillcrest Dairies. And we did the advertising. It was a half-hour program on a Sunday evening. For which I think the fee was something like about $6.

Well, it had to be before 34. Before 34. Yeah, yeah. Because 32, when the banks closed. When the banks closed. Really? About 32. About 32. When the banks closed. We stayed there, but we didn't stay too much longer. And Lelke was there. And Pinky was there. And they kept Lelke because they only had four or five people. And they let Pinky go.
